Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're kicking off our internal checklist for the Redwood private deployment in our West-2 VPC and need to lock down the exact IP/port/hostname allowlist and the outbound/egress expectations from your control plane and any external telemetry/metrics endpoints. Procurement also asked for a short evidence bundle we can pass to our Security Ops.

Concretely, can you provide:
- A canonical list of IP ranges (and whether they are static or may change) that our firewall should permit for control-plane callbacks and health-checks.
- Ports and protocols required (including any outbound DNS/TLS exceptions).
- Guidance on NATing (do you require source-IP preservation or is SNAT fine?).
- Any known external endpoints (metrics, error reporting, license checks) and whether they can be proxied through our egress proxy.

We're on a somewhat tight timeline — would appreciate details and any checklist template we can reuse. I've attached our internal safelist template for your convenience.

Pat

Pat — thanks, this is helpful. Looping in Laura (networking) and Marissa (customer ops) so we can provide a concise evidence pack.

High level: Redwood's private endpoint control plane expects a small, largely stable set of egress IPs for the control path; however Runtime (model-serving) egress depends on the deployment mode — for fully private (VPC with no internet egress) you can proxy control-plane traffic through your NAT/proxy. A few specifics below; Laura will follow up with the exact CIDRs and port matrix.

Quick notes:
- Control plane: static-ish IPs documented and updated in the ticket. We publish notice 14 days before any change.
- Health checks/Callbacks: TLS 443 outbound to control plane hostnames; SNI required.
- Metrics/Telemetry: optional; can be disabled for high-compliance customers. If enabled, metrics endpoints are reachable over TLS and can be proxied.
- SNAT: acceptable. We do not require source-IP preservation for telemetry; however for some debug diagnostics having stable egress IPs helps expedite support.

Laura — can you paste the current CIDR list and any guidance on egress binding? Marissa — we'll need to prepare the evidence checklist and a one‑page guidance doc for Pinebrook's Security Ops.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Pat / Team,

Below is the operational guidance and the current set of addresses we ask customers to allow for control-plane interactions. Note this is for the private endpoint control-plane and baked-in observability endpoints; model-serving nodes (the Dedicated pool) sit in your private network when in Private mode and do not require additional outbound to Redwood unless you opt into managed telemetry.

1) Control-plane egress (required for management/rollouts/fallbacks):
- Hostnames: control-api-us.redwood.ai, auth-us.redwood.ai
- IP blocks (current): 34.210.176.0/24, 52.12.48.0/24, 3.231.92.0/25
  - Status: these are allocated to our control-plane fleet in us-west-2 and are considered "stable-ish". We communicate changes via the ticket above with 14-day notice.
- Ports: 443 (TLS); outbound only.
- Protocol: HTTPS with SNI; client TLS required.

2) Optional telemetry/metrics (can be disabled):
- Hostnames: metrics-collector.redwood.ai
- IPs: 13.57.22.0/25
- Ports: 443 (TLS).
- Note: If you proxy metrics through your egress, ensure the proxy preserves SNI and forwards TLS (TLS passthrough preferred) — otherwise some features (agent identity) will be degraded.

3) DNS and certificate checks:
- Allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to your internal resolver or to the internet resolver of choice.
- Distrust of external DNS: If you operate a split-horizon resolver, ensure control-api-us.redwood.ai resolves to public IPs from the agent/NAT plane.

4) NATing / SNAT guidance:
- SNAT is acceptable for all control-plane calls.
- If you need expedited troubleshooting, set up a small pinned egress IP (your proxy NAT pool) and provide it to us; we can add temporary allowlist entries on the Redwood side for diagnostics.

5) Outbound ports for additional services (rare):
- Time sync (NTP): UDP 123 to your preferred pool (we do not require direct NTP to Redwood).
- CRL/OCSP: 80/443 to various CA endpoints — generally not blocked long term; if your firewall blocks these, certificate validation may fail.

6) Evidence pack and attestations we can provide:
- Signed CIDR snapshot (CSV) for the IP blocks above.
- TLS cert fingerprints for control-api hostnames.
- Operational note: we provide 14-day change notice and a signed changelog for enterprise customers.

Attachment: egress-evidence-checklist.pdf (pdf)

If you want, we can run a short connectivity test (curl + TLS handshake) from your staging subnet to validate NAT/proxy behavior next week.

Laura Bennett
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
